Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Town, shops & places

town hall noun

also city hall, council offices, municipal building, townhall

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.2.50: in cūriā Syrācūsīs
Traupman 173, 396
M-O s.v. city hall, town hall

cūria, cūriae f.

noun, first declension

town hall; classically a council house

The house where a council met: at Rome the senate house, and the council houses of other towns too, such as the one at Syracuse that its people called the bouleuterion (Cic. Verr. 2.2.50; Lewis & Short). Traupman gives it for a city hall; Morgan–Owens for a city or town hall, as Vives used it of the house where the magistrates of Valencia met.

Other words

  • cūria mūnicipālis — town hall

    noun phrase: cūria with the adjective mūnicipālis · also used · modern · Traupman 396; M-O s.v. city hall, town hall

    Mūnicipālis, of a mūnicipium, a self-governing town, is classical (Cic., Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • effundī in vestibulō cūriae jussit ānulōs aureōs

    he had the gold rings tipped out in the entrance of the council house (at Carthage)Liv. 23.12.1

See also council, mayor, town, city.

SourcesLewis & Short: curia · Lewis & Short: municipalis

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. city hall, town hall; legislature: building in which a legislature or municipal council convenes.
